entries.claim: Pre-registering hypotheses and analysis plans reduces selective reporting and p-hacking by fixing researcher degrees of freedom before data are seen
Undisclosed flexibility in data collection and analysis inflates false-positive rates
Omitting a confounder biases the estimated association; adjusting for it (or blocking the backdoor path) removes that component of bias
entries.locator: Hernán & Robins, Causal Inference: What If, Chapters 7-8
entries.notes: Basis of equations 1-2, figure 2 and section 04

entries.claim: A structured checklist of degrees of freedom across planning, running, analysing and reporting helps avoid p-hacking
entries.locator: Wicherts et al. (2016), Frontiers in Psychology 7, 1832
entries.notes: Supports the reporting checklist in section 05

entries.claim: The exercise/BMI dataset is deterministic and constructed with a true exercise coefficient of -0.5; the unadjusted slope is -1.335 and the age-adjusted slope is -0.5
entries.notes: Computed by hand and by the standard-library code in section 07; reproducible
